name: B'dazzled Blue
lede: B'dazzled Blue is a Crayola crayon name, a pun on *bedazzled*, for a mid sapphire blue from the company's metallic line around 2000.

sections.title: Where the name comes from
sections.body: Crayola introduced a box of metallic crayons in 2000 and renamed the line Metallic FX the following year; B'dazzled Blue is on the color list for both years [1]. The names in that line came from a naming contest open to residents of the United States and Canada, judged by Crayola's parent company, Binney and Smith [1]. Some winning names are credited to named people; B'dazzled Blue's is not, so who coined it is undocumented [1]. Crayola names have a history of their own: in 1958 the company renamed its [[prussian-blue|Prussian blue]] crayon [[midnight-blue|Midnight Blue]] after teachers said children could not relate to Prussian history [5].

sections.title: A flat swatch for a shiny crayon
sections.body: The hex value most lists give, #2E5894, comes via Wikipedia from Crayola [2]. It can only be an approximation: the real crayon has a metallic shimmer that no flat screen color can show [1][2]. As a flat color it is a mid sapphire blue, almost identical to [[dusk-blue]], [[sapphire-crayola]] and the modern pigment [[yinmn-blue]], all within three units [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,531 paintings, a color within six units of it covers at least five per cent of the canvas in 58, led by Matisse's *The Conversation*, where it fills nearly half the picture [4]. As photographed, and long before the crayon existed [4].

disambiguation: B'dazzled Blue (Crayola, metallic) vs Dusk Blue (xkcd survey name): nearly the same screen color, unrelated names.
